about.title: Personal Injury Help in McFarland, California
about.longDescription: McFarland sits along a stretch of Kern County where daily life runs through a handful of key roads — Elmo Highway, SR-99, Driver Road, and Garzoli Avenue carry the bulk of local traffic, and public records show these corridors account for the highest collision counts in town. The most recent full-year data recorded one traffic death in McFarland, a reminder that even a town this size isn't immune to serious crashes. If you or someone you love was hurt in a collision here, sorting out what comes next — medical bills, missed work, insurance calls — can feel like too much to handle alone. We provide free case reviews to injured people in McFarland. We handle personal injury claims directly, and our team works on contingency, meaning there's no cost to you unless we recover money on your behalf. Our goal is simple: help you understand your options and get you talking to someone who can actually help, without adding to your stress or your bills. Reach out and let us review your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of an injury to file a claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity is involved. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages — like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life — in ordinary injury cases. That matters when the physical and emotional toll outweighs the medical bills.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you win or settle. There's no retainer, no hourly fee, and no financial risk in finding out where you stand.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in McFarland?
items.answer: In most California injury cases, you have two years from the date of the incident to file a lawsuit. If a government agency or public road authority is involved, that deadline can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth checking your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your total award is reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't wiped out entirely.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in McFarland?
items.answer: Public collision records show the highest counts along Elmo Highway, SR-99, Driver Road, and Garzoli Avenue, with reports tending to peak on Wednesdays between 10 a.m. and noon. These are neutral, publicly reported counts, not a judgment about any particular road.
